title: Chicken Cacciatore
description: This Chicken Cacciatore has the robust flavor this Italian favorite is known for, but is far easier to make than traditional chicken cacciatore. This stovetop one-skillet chicken stew is simmered with tomatoes, and vegetables. The pleasing aroma will have your family gathered around the table. Cacciatore means “hunter's style” in Italian and would typically be made in the woods over a fire with whatever was caught or harvested that day.
ingredients: 4 chicken thighs skin on and bone in
8+ oz mushrooms (like Baby Bella, or home grown from Andrea) sliced
½ cup chicken broth or red wine
directions: Season the chicken thighs with Italian seasonings, salt and pepper.

Heat a large skillet with oil on a medium flame, add the chicken thighs skin down and cook for 5-6 minutes until they turn golden, then flip and cook on the other side for 3-4 minutes. Transfer them to a plate and set aside.
To the same skillet add onions, minced garlic, and mushrooms. Sauté for 4-5 minutes and then add the sliced bell pepper and cook for 2 more minutes.
Stir in the little bit of stock, tomato paste, canned tomatoes and juice, Italian seasonings, (maybe extra dashes of thyme and oregano), salt and pepper. Bring it to a boil.

Arrange the chicken thighs back to the skillet and add olives and capers. Cover and cook for about 30 minutes until the chicken thighs are cooked through on a low flame. (Even better: you could also do this in the oven at 350 degrees, with or without a cover, maybe broiling without a cover for the final 5-7 minutes.)
Once done, garnish the chicken cacciatore with freshly chopped parsley or basil (or nothing or anything at hand) and serve with pasta, polenta, rice, or mashed potatoes.
